main_body: A flat brick/stone wall-face texture tile (running-bond stone blocks with mortar lines), drawn as a front-facing surface pattern filling the whole 64x48 area
top_band: none; the column scan shows a repeating pattern of a light 1px edge row, mid-tone fill rows, and dark mortar rows, with no distinct horizontal top surface
evidence: The candidate is a terrain wall-face tile. It is a repeating brick pattern seen face-on, with no standing object, top surface, or footprint. The kind is terrain, so it is a tiling texture rather than a standing object, but the drawing is a pure front elevation of a wall with only 1px highlights and mortar lines. Under strict rules, with no 3/4 top band, it fails.

style.evidence: The references are grass and paving ground patches, while the candidate is a brick wall pattern, so the kind match is loose. The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 26 for grass and 7 for paving. It is on par with paving on colour count but far below grass. The dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the mortar and outline read as a neutral grey-brown line rather than a tinted material tone. Texture is limited to a few sparse speckle dots on each brick, with no grain or per-stone shading. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but the bricks are uniform and repetitive. Overall it is shallower than the Beodeul standard.
